questoes.pergunta: The rule "every new route needs an integration test" must apply to all developers in the repository. Where should it live?
opcoes: In each developer's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
In the `CLAUDE.md` at the project root, versioned in git
In the `CLAUDE.local.md` at the project root
In the project's auto memory (`MEMORY.md`)
questoes.explicacao: Team instructions go in the project's CLAUDE.md (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), which is versioned and reaches everyone when they clone.
feedbacks: Tempting because it 'works', but the user file is personal: each developer would have to copy it by hand, and anyone who doesn't won't get the rule.
Correct: the project's CLAUDE.md is shared via git and loaded for everyone.
CLAUDE.local.md is personal and goes in .gitignore, so the team doesn't receive it.
Auto memory is written by Claude itself and is local to the machine; it's not a channel for team rules.

questoes.pergunta: A repository has `AGENTS.md` (used by another coding agent) and also `CLAUDE.md` at the root. What does Claude Code load by default, and how do you unify them?
opcoes: It loads both and concatenates them; there's nothing to do
It loads only AGENTS.md, because it's the open standard
It loads whichever was modified most recently
It loads only CLAUDE.md; to make use of AGENTS.md, import it with `@AGENTS.md` inside CLAUDE.md
questoes.explicacao: AGENTS.md is only read when there is no CLAUDE.md. With both, CLAUDE.md wins; the simple way to have a single source is `@AGENTS.md` in CLAUDE.md.
feedbacks: Sounds reasonable, but by default AGENTS.md is ignored when a CLAUDE.md exists.
It reverses the rule: CLAUDE.md is the one that takes priority.
There's no criterion based on modification date.
Correct: CLAUDE.md wins; the @import brings AGENTS.md along with it.

questoes.pergunta: A file `.claude/rules/tests.md` has the frontmatter `paths: ["**/*Tests.cs"]`. When does it enter the context?
opcoes: When Claude reads or edits a file that matches the glob
Always, at the start of the session, like CLAUDE.md
Only when the user types `/tests`
Only when an Explore subagent is triggered
questoes.explicacao: A rule with `paths` is conditional: it loads when Claude touches (Read/Write/Edit) a file that matches the pattern. Without `paths`, it always loads.
feedbacks: Correct: conditional loading by path.
That's the behavior of a rule WITHOUT `paths`.
It confuses a rule with a skill/command; rules aren't invoked with `/`.
It has nothing to do with subagents.

questoes.pergunta: The repository has `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md`, with different contents. What happens with `/deploy`?
opcoes: Both run in sequence
The command wins, because it's the older format
The skill wins
Claude Code refuses to start because of the name conflict
questoes.explicacao: Commands and skills have been merged; both create `/deploy`. In a name conflict, the skill wins.
feedbacks: The contents aren't combined; only one wins.
That's the trap: the legacy format still works, but it loses in a conflict.
Correct.
There's no startup error because of this.

questoes.pergunta: Claude triggered the `/deploy-prod` skill on its own during a conversation about deployment. Which adjustment fixes this directly?
opcoes: Remove the skill's `description`
Add `disable-model-invocation: true` to the frontmatter
Add `user-invocable: false` to the frontmatter
Write "don't run a deploy without being asked" in CLAUDE.md
questoes.explicacao: `disable-model-invocation: true` makes it so only the user can invoke the skill: the right choice for actions with side effects.
feedbacks: A hack: the description is there for guidance; without it the skill is poorly documented and the control isn't explicit.
Correct: only you invoke it.
It's the opposite: `user-invocable: false` hides it from the menu and lets ONLY Claude invoke it.
A prompt instruction is probabilistic; there's a deterministic control in the frontmatter.

questoes.pergunta: What does `context: fork` do in a skill's frontmatter?
opcoes: Runs the skill in an isolated subagent, which doesn't see the conversation history, and returns the result
Creates a fork of the git repository before executing
Duplicates the current session so the user can compare two responses
Makes the skill be reread from disk on every turn
questoes.explicacao: `context: fork` runs the skill in a subagent with its own context (optionally of the type defined in `agent`); the conversation history doesn't go along.
feedbacks: Correct.
A mix-up with a git 'fork'; it has nothing to do with the repository.
It's not a session branch for comparing responses.
The skill's body isn't reread; and that has nothing to do with `context: fork`.

questoes.pergunta: The same scalar key (e.g., `model`) is set in `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, and `.claude/settings.local.json`, with no managed settings and no CLI flag. Which value applies?
opcoes: The one in `~/.claude/settings.json`, because it belongs to the user
The one in `.claude/settings.json`, because it belongs to the team
The first file read in alphabetical order
The one in `.claude/settings.local.json`
questoes.explicacao: Precedence: managed > command line > local project > shared project > user. Without managed/CLI, local wins.
feedbacks: The user level has the LOWEST precedence.
The shared file loses to the local project file.
There's no alphabetical order in precedence.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: The project's `.claude/settings.json` has `deny: ["Bash(git push *)"]`, and one developer's `settings.local.json` has `allow: ["Bash(git push *)"]`. Does `git push` run without being blocked?
opcoes: Yes, because local takes precedence over project
Yes, but only after a confirmation prompt
No: deny is evaluated before allow, and allow doesn't carve out an exception to a deny
It depends on which rule is more specific
questoes.explicacao: Rules are evaluated deny → ask → allow; the first match decides, regardless of level or specificity.
feedbacks: Level precedence applies to scalar keys; permission lists are merged and deny wins.
It doesn't turn into a prompt: deny blocks.
Correct.
Specificity doesn't change the evaluation order.

questoes.pergunta: What does the permission rule `Bash(dotnet test *)` allow?
opcoes: Any command that starts with `dotnet test`, such as `dotnet test --filter Unit`
Only the exact command `dotnet test *` with a literal asterisk
Any `dotnet` command, including `dotnet publish`
Only tests, because Claude Code understands the semantics of "test"
questoes.explicacao: The trailing ` *` performs prefix matching. The `:*` form (e.g., `Bash(npm run test:*)`) is equivalent.
feedbacks: Correct.
The asterisk is a wildcard, not a literal.
The prefix is `dotnet test`, not `dotnet`.
The rule is text matching, not semantics.

questoes.pergunta: For which task is plan mode the most appropriate choice?
opcoes: Adding a null check on a line pointed out by a stack trace
Migrating the logging library used in 45 files, with two possible approaches
Renaming a constant in a single file
Fixing a typo in a log message
questoes.explicacao: Plan mode is for multi-file or architectural changes, or ones with several valid approaches: it explores, proposes, and only edits after approval.
feedbacks: Small, clear scope: direct execution.
Correct.
Trivial; plan mode would just add friction.
Trivial; direct execution.

questoes.pergunta: Which statements about the built-in Explore and Plan subagents are true? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: They can edit files when the parent is in acceptEdits
They are read-only
They inherit the full history of the main conversation
They keep the main context clean, returning only the conclusion of the exploration
They must be defined manually in `.claude/agents/` before use
questoes.explicacao: Explore and Plan are built-in, read-only, and work in an isolated context, returning only the result.
feedbacks: Write/Edit are denied to them, whatever the parent's mode.
Correct: read-only.
A subagent has isolated context; it doesn't inherit the history.
Correct: that's their main value.
They're built-in; `.claude/agents/` is for custom ones.

questoes.pergunta: A custom subagent has `permissionMode: bypassPermissions`, but the main session is in `default`. What happens?
opcoes: The subagent runs in bypass, because its frontmatter takes priority
The main session switches to bypass as well
Claude Code refuses to load the subagent
The subagent doesn't get bypass: it can't escalate beyond the main conversation's mode
questoes.explicacao: The parent's permission flows down: a subagent doesn't escalate privileges. A subagent with bypassPermissions in a default session doesn't get bypass.
feedbacks: That's exactly what the rule prevents.
Nothing flows up from the subagent to the parent.
It loads normally; it just doesn't get the requested mode.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A developer wants to know which files call the `CalculateShipping` method. Which built-in tool is the most appropriate?
opcoes: Glob with `**/*.cs`
Read on every `.cs` file
Grep for `CalculateShipping`
WebFetch on the internal documentation
questoes.explicacao: Grep searches content; Glob only finds files by name/pattern.
feedbacks: Glob lists files by name; it doesn't look at content.
Reading everything up front is the classic anti-pattern: it burns context.
Correct.
It doesn't answer where the code calls the method.

questoes.pergunta: `Edit` failed because the snippet `return null;` appears 7 times in the file. What is the best next action?
opcoes: Expand the `old_string` with surrounding lines until it's unique (or use `replace_all` if the intent is to change all of them)
Repeat the same Edit until it works
Switch to Bash with `sed -i` without looking at the file
Give up and ask the user to edit it manually
questoes.explicacao: Edit requires a unique snippet. Expand the snippet's context, use `replace_all` when changing all occurrences, or read and rewrite the file.
feedbacks: Correct.
The same input will fail the same way.
It works around the problem blindly and may change the wrong occurrences.
Unnecessary: there's a simple fix.

questoes.pergunta: Which items enter the context right at the start of the session, regardless of which files Claude touches? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: The `CLAUDE.md` at the project root
The `CLAUDE.md` in a subdirectory below the working directory
A rule in `.claude/rules/` without `paths` frontmatter
A rule in `.claude/rules/` with `paths: ["src/api/**"]`
The full body of every skill in the project
questoes.explicacao: The project's CLAUDE.md and rules without `paths` load at startup. A subdirectory's CLAUDE.md and rules with `paths` load on demand; for skills, only the description is available until invocation.
feedbacks: Correct.
A subdirectory below loads on demand, when Claude touches files there.
Correct.
With `paths`, it only loads when a matching file is touched.
A skill's body only enters when it's invoked; before that, only the description guides automatic loading.
